Name: SA account is disabled
Description: The built-in SA (System Administrator) account is a well-known target for brute force attacks. It should be disabled when not required.
Rationale: Disabling the SA account reduces the attack surface for credential attacks against a known login.
Query: SELECT CAST(is_disabled AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.server_principals WHERE name = 'sa'
RemediationText: Disable the SA account: ALTER LOGIN [sa] DISABLE;

Name: SA account has been renamed
Description: The SA account should be renamed to a non-obvious name to reduce automated attack risk.
Rationale: Renaming SA prevents attackers from using the well-known account name in credential attacks.
Query: SELECT name FROM sys.server_principals WHERE sid = 0x01
RemediationText: Rename SA: ALTER LOGIN [sa] WITH NAME = [SysAdmin_Renamed];

Name: Windows-only authentication mode enabled
Description: SQL Server mixed-mode authentication allows SQL logins which are weaker than Windows-integrated authentication.
Rationale: Windows authentication leverages Kerberos/NTLM and Windows account policies. SQL logins bypass these controls.
Query: SELECT CAST(SERVERPROPERTY('IsIntegratedSecurityOnly') AS VARCHAR)
RemediationText: Switch to Windows Authentication only in SQL Server Properties > Security, then restart the SQL Server service.

Name: BUILTIN\Administrators not a SQL Server login
Description: The BUILTIN\Administrators group should not have a SQL Server login, as all local admins would gain SQL access.
Rationale: Removing this login enforces least-privilege: not every local admin needs SQL Server sysadmin rights.
Query: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.server_principals WHERE name = 'BUILTIN\Administrators'
RemediationText: DROP LOGIN [BUILTIN\Administrators]; — ensure other sysadmin logins exist first.

Name: Guest user CONNECT revoked in all user databases
Description: The guest user should not have CONNECT permission in user databases.
Rationale: Allowing guest CONNECT enables any SQL Server login to access the database, bypassing per-user access control.
Query: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.databases d JOIN sys.database_permissions p ON p.grantee_principal_id = DATABASE_PRINCIPAL_ID('guest') WHERE p.permission_name = 'CONNECT' AND d.name NOT IN ('master','tempdb','msdb')
RemediationText: For each affected database: USE [dbname]; REVOKE CONNECT FROM guest;

Name: xp_cmdshell is disabled
Description: xp_cmdshell allows execution of Windows OS commands directly from T-SQL.
Rationale: xp_cmdshell is a critical attack vector that allows OS-level command execution if SQL Server is compromised.
Query: SELECT CAST(value_in_use AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.configurations WHERE name = 'xp_cmdshell'
RemediationText: EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 0; RECONFIGURE;

Name: Ad Hoc Distributed Queries disabled
Description: Ad Hoc Distributed Queries allow OPENROWSET and OPENDATASOURCE functions which can access external data sources.
Rationale: Disabling reduces the ability to exfiltrate data or access external malicious resources from SQL.
Query: SELECT CAST(value_in_use AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.configurations WHERE name = 'Ad Hoc Distributed Queries'
RemediationText: EXEC sp_configure 'Ad Hoc Distributed Queries', 0; RECONFIGURE;

Name: CLR Enabled is disabled
Description: SQL Server CLR integration enables .NET code to execute inside SQL Server. This is rarely required.
Rationale: CLR code can be used to escape SQL sandbox constraints and execute arbitrary code.
Query: SELECT CAST(value_in_use AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.configurations WHERE name = 'clr enabled'
RemediationText: EXEC sp_configure 'clr enabled', 0; RECONFIGURE;

Name: Cross DB Ownership Chaining disabled
Description: Cross-database ownership chaining allows a stored procedure in one database to access objects in another database.
Rationale: Enables privilege escalation across database boundaries when exploited.
Query: SELECT CAST(value_in_use AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.configurations WHERE name = 'cross db ownership chaining'
RemediationText: EXEC sp_configure 'cross db ownership chaining', 0; RECONFIGURE;

Name: Database Mail XPs disabled
Description: Database Mail XPs enable sending email from SQL Server. Should be disabled if not needed.
Rationale: Can be abused to exfiltrate data or used as a C2 channel in a compromised environment.
Query: SELECT CAST(value_in_use AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.configurations WHERE name = 'Database Mail XPs'
RemediationText: EXEC sp_configure 'Database Mail XPs', 0; RECONFIGURE;

Name: OLE Automation Procedures disabled
Description: OLE Automation stored procedures (sp_OA*) allow COM object creation from T-SQL.
Rationale: COM automation from SQL Server can be leveraged to execute arbitrary code.
Query: SELECT CAST(value_in_use AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.configurations WHERE name = 'Ole Automation Procedures'
RemediationText: EXEC sp_configure 'Ole Automation Procedures', 0; RECONFIGURE;

Name: Remote Access disabled
Description: The remote access option controls execution of stored procedures from remote SQL Server instances.
Rationale: Remote access is deprecated and can be exploited for lateral movement between SQL Server instances.
Query: SELECT CAST(value_in_use AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.configurations WHERE name = 'remote access'
RemediationText: EXEC sp_configure 'remote access', 0; RECONFIGURE; -- requires SQL Server restart

Name: Scan for Startup Procedures disabled
Description: Startup stored procedures execute automatically when SQL Server starts.
Rationale: An attacker who can create procedures could establish persistence through auto-executing startup procs.
Query: SELECT CAST(value_in_use AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.configurations WHERE name = 'scan for startup procs'
RemediationText: EXEC sp_configure 'scan for startup procs', 0; RECONFIGURE;

Name: TRUSTWORTHY is OFF on all non-system databases
Description: When TRUSTWORTHY is ON, objects in the database can access external resources using the database owner's context.
Rationale: If a database owner has sysadmin rights, a TRUSTWORTHY database can be leveraged to escalate privileges.
Query: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.databases WHERE is_trustworthy_on = 1 AND name NOT IN ('msdb')
RemediationText: For each affected DB: ALTER DATABASE [dbname] SET TRUSTWORTHY OFF;

Name: Login auditing set to Success and Failure
Description: SQL Server should log both successful and failed login attempts.
Rationale: Without login failure logging, brute force attempts are invisible. Without success logging, unauthorized access is undetected.
Query: SELECT CAST(SERVERPROPERTY('AuditLevel') AS VARCHAR)
RemediationText: Set via SQL Server Management Studio: Server Properties > Security > Login auditing > Both failed and successful logins. Then restart SQL Server service.

Name: SQL Server Audit object created and enabled
Description: A SQL Server Audit object should be configured to capture security-relevant events.
Rationale: The built-in audit infrastructure provides tamper-evident logging that is more reliable than application-level logging.
Query: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.server_audits WHERE is_state_enabled = 1
RemediationText: Create and enable a Server Audit: CREATE SERVER AUDIT [SecurityAudit] TO FILE (FILEPATH = 'C:\Audit\'); ALTER SERVER AUDIT [SecurityAudit] WITH (STATE = ON);

Name: Failed logins captured by audit
Description: Audit specifications should include the FAILED_LOGIN_GROUP.
Rationale: Captures credential attacks for forensic investigation and alerting.
Query: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.server_audit_specification_details WHERE audit_action_name = 'FAILED_LOGIN_GROUP'
RemediationText: Add FAILED_LOGIN_GROUP to a server audit specification.

Name: Force Encryption enabled (TLS required for all connections)
Description: SQL Server should require TLS encryption for all client connections.
Rationale: Unencrypted SQL connections expose credentials and query data to network interception.
Query: SELECT CAST(value_data AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.registry_values WHERE registry_key LIKE '%SuperSocketNetLib%' AND value_name = 'ForceEncryption'
RemediationText: Enable 'Force Encryption' in SQL Server Configuration Manager > SQL Server Network Configuration > Protocols > Properties > Force Encryption = Yes. Requires SQL Server restart.

Name: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) on sensitive databases
Description: TDE encrypts database files at rest, protecting against physical media theft.
Rationale: Without TDE, database .mdf/.ldf files can be attached to another SQL instance and read without credentials.
Query: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS VARCHAR) FROM sys.databases WHERE is_encrypted = 0 AND name NOT IN ('master','model','msdb','tempdb')
RemediationText: Enable TDE per database: CREATE DATABASE ENCRYPTION KEY WITH ALGORITHM = AES_256 ENCRYPTION BY SERVER CERTIFICATE [TDECert]; ALTER DATABASE [dbname] SET ENCRYPTION ON;

Name: Error log retention at least 12 files
Description: SQL Server should retain at least 12 error log files to support forensic investigation.
Rationale: Log retention below 12 files means logs roll over and erase evidence of past incidents.
Query: DECLARE @n INT; EXEC master.dbo.xp_instance_regread N'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE', N'Software\Microsoft\MSSQLServer\MSSQLServer', N'NumErrorLogs', @n OUTPUT; SELECT CAST(ISNULL(@n,6) AS VARCHAR)
RemediationText: EXEC xp_instance_regwrite N'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE', N'Software\Microsoft\MSSQLServer\MSSQLServer', N'NumErrorLogs', REG_DWORD, 12;

Name: SQL Server Agent jobs owned by non-SA accounts
Description: SQL Agent jobs should not be owned by the SA account or sysadmin-level logins.
Rationale: Jobs owned by privileged accounts execute in that security context, enabling privilege escalation.
Query: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS VARCHAR) FROM msdb.dbo.sysjobs j JOIN sys.server_principals p ON p.sid = j.owner_sid WHERE p.is_sysadmin = 1
RemediationText: For each affected job: EXEC msdb.dbo.sp_update_job @job_name = N'JobName', @owner_login_name = N'non_privileged_login';
